verdict.rationale: PayPal documents its own MCP server, available both locally and as remote hosted endpoints, that "lets merchants use natural language with their favorite MCP clients." It is backed by an agent-tool inventory covering catalog, invoices, payments, refunds, disputes, subscriptions, shipment tracking and reporting, with a sample natural-language prompt for each tool. Natural-language operation does require bringing an external MCP client or LLM, and it is scoped to merchant back-office tasks. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the natural-language commands work reliably, coverage of consumer-account operations, a first-party built-in conversational interface not dependent on third-party agent clients.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: PayPal built an MCP server that lets merchants use natural language with their favorite MCP clients.
PayPal recently launched a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that customers can use to access the power of PayPal using natural language with any AI agent.
Each tool documents parameters and a sample prompt.
sample prompt "Give me insights on my sales data from 01/01/2025 to 02/01/2025 using daily time intervals"
